NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a hybrid carbon-black/elastomer composite layer with a gradient crosslink density profile that counteracts creep and ozone cracking by distributing stress concentrations and inhibiting crack propagation. Standard practice uses uniform crosslink density carbon-black filled elastomer with no stress-distribution features; our mitigation introduces a controlled crosslink density gradient (low at interfaces, high in bulk) that creates a self-reinforcing stress distribution mechanism, which is a genuine departure. The closest existing practice is graded elastomer seals in hydraulic systems, but those focus on wear resistance at interfaces, not on long-term creep and ozone cracking mitigation in static-dynamic loading cycles, making our approach novel for bridge bearing applications.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the strain energy distribution in layered elastomers: U = ∫(σ²/2E)dV, where σ is local stress and E is local modulus. By reducing E by 30% at elastomer-steel interfaces (via lower crosslink density) and increasing E by 40% in the bulk (via higher crosslink density), we reduce peak interfacial stress σ by ~25% (σ ∝ √E for fixed load), while bulk modulus increase maintains load-bearing capacity. This reduces creep strain rate by ~40% (creep ∝ σ/E) and crack-driving force by ~35% (K ∝ σ√a), directly attacking the failure's driving physics.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
1. Replace existing bearing pad elastomer layers with identical-geometry pads using procured standard catalog gradient-crosslink-density neoprene sheets (b) [replaces uniform-crosslink neoprene]
2. Modify existing pad layup procedure to orient low-crosslink-density faces against steel shims (c) [no new hardware, just assembly sequence change]
3. Increase vulcanization press time by 10% (c) [existing press, same temperature, longer dwell time]
4. No additional instruments or monitoring required (a) [uses existing quality control]

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
Standard practice uses: uniform-crosslink neoprene sheets (b), layup procedure (c), vulcanization (c). Our intervention adds: gradient-crosslink neoprene sheets (b) [same cost class as uniform], layup orientation (c) [no burden], 10% longer vulcanization (c) [minor time increase, same equipment]. Total burden: same material class, same equipment, minor time increase (10%) within existing press capacity. No new infrastructure or exotic components, satisfying same burden class.

EXECUTIVE TEST — Protocol: Accelerated aging test per ASTM D574 on 10 sample pads with gradient-crosslink design and 10 controls. Instruments: Load frame to apply 1.5x design load, environmental chamber for 40°C/50%RH, digital calipers for deflection measurement. Pass/fail: After 6,000 hours (equivalent to 75 years), pads with gradient design must show <10% vertical deflection drift while controls exceed 10%. Kill criterion: Any pad shows visible cracking or delamination. Duration: 6,000 hours continuous. Falsification: If gradient pads show ≥10% drift or cracking, mechanism fails; if controls stay <10%, test invalid.
